methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $100M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Ocean Infinity, a growth-stage maritime technology company founded by Oliver Plunkett, has raised over $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a constrained comparable universe: one identifiable private peer (Orbital Marine Power) and no public ocean-sector benchmarks, limiting triangulation breadth.

Stage-progression methodology was the applicable valuation approach. Using the $100M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage advancement, the implied valuation reached $120M. This represents a measured escalation from cumulative capital deployed, absent material revenue or profitability data to anchor alternative approaches such as revenue multiples or DCF analysis.

The triangulated valuation range spans $102M (low) to $138M (median $120M), reflecting conservative bounds around the stage-progression result. The narrow method count (one applicable technique) and sparse comparable set introduce material uncertainty. Without public comps or additional private transactions in ocean and maritime technology, calibration against market pricing remains constrained. Key uncertainties include unit economics, path to profitability, and competitive positioning relative to Orbital Marine Power. Investors should regard this range as indicative pending access to fuller financial disclosure or expansion of the peer dataset.
